messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear constrained GMRF
parts:
On 11 Oct 2013, at 11:53, xiao guo <xiao.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
I had a try. e.g. k and n are both of order 10^3 ..  the additional cost is significant ( overnight running .. not ended yet )

As others already answered, enforcing a large number of (exact) constraints is computationally infeasible.  If the constraints are sufficiently sparse, they can be implemented as "soft" constraints via in the observation likelihood instead.

I wonder if A in Ax=e here is sparse matrix (however in inla.spde2.matern, extraconstr has to be "matrix", cannot be signed with "dgCMatrix" class sparse matrix, right?), would it be quicker?

What types of constraint are you trying to enforce, and why? Without that information it's virtually impossible for us to provide a relevant answer.

Finn

 
Many thanks!
Xiao Guo
